draft.title: The internal environment
card: The internal environment is the set of factors inside a business that its owners and managers can control. Customers, suppliers and competitors sit outside the business, so they are not part of it.
the goods or services the business chooses to sell, and where it chooses to operate. It can add a new product or move to new premises.
the people, money and equipment the business has. Managers decide how many staff to hire and train, how to spend funds and what equipment to buy.
how the business is led and organised, and its culture: the shared values and habits of its staff. These shape how well it responds to change.
draft.remember: If the business can decide it from the inside, it is internal. If it happens outside, it is external.

a.q: Which of these is part of a business's internal environment?
opts: The skills of the staff it employs
A rise in interest rates across Australia
A shift in what consumers like to buy
a.why: Staff are one of the business's own resources, and it controls who it hires and how it trains them. A new competitor is close to the business, but it is a separate firm outside its control, so it is external.
a.clue: Which one could the business change by its own decision?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Ballarat. Which of these is part of her bakery's internal environment?
opts: The friendly culture among her bakers
The price her supplier charges for flour
The loyalty of her regular customers
The prices set by a rival bakery
b.why: The culture among her own staff is inside the business, and Priya shapes it through how she leads. Customer loyalty is tempting because it feels like part of the bakery, but customers are outside the business, so they belong to the external environment.
b.clue: Are customers and suppliers inside or outside the business?

a.best: The skills of the staff it employs

b.best: The friendly culture among her bakers
